summary.text: Friction is the force that resists solid surfaces, fluid layers or material elements sliding or grinding against each other.
Dry friction comes in two kinds: static friction between surfaces that are not moving and kinetic friction between surfaces that are.
Friction turns mechanical energy into heat and wears parts down, and its losses account for about a fifth of the world's energy use.

items.prompt: You push a heavy couch. Getting it to budge feels harder than keeping it sliding. What fits this?

options.label: Resting and moving surfaces meet different friction, and moving is easier
Friction vanishes once any sliding has started
Gravity pulls harder on couches that are not moving
The floor presses back harder once the couch moves

items.explain: Dry friction divides into static and kinetic, and an ancient observer noted it is easier to further the motion of a moving body than to move one at rest.

items.prompt: You rub your cold hands together and they warm up. What is happening to the energy of the rubbing?

options.label: It is stored as extra chemical energy
Some of it turns into heat
It is destroyed by the rubbing
It becomes extra speed in your skin

items.explain: When surfaces in contact move relative to each other, some mechanical energy is transformed into heat and other forms of dissipation.

items.prompt: A mechanic puts oil between two metal parts that rub together. What kind of friction is that?

options.label: Dry friction between two bare solid surfaces
Skin friction caused by a body moving through air
Fluid friction between the layers of a separating liquid
Internal friction inside one deforming solid

items.explain: Lubricated friction is a case of fluid friction where a lubricant fluid separates two solid surfaces.

items.prompt: The brake pads on a bike get thinner every year. Which consequence of friction is that?

options.label: Tribology, a way the parts are studied
Static friction, which pulls the pads together
Adhesion, which makes the pads grow
Wear, which can degrade or damage parts

items.explain: Many types of friction cause wear, which may lead to performance degradation or damage to components.

items.prompt: Why do engineers often use measurements rather than calculate friction from first principles?

options.label: Friction has no cause that physicists can name
Many interacting contributors make a direct calculation difficult
Friction behaves differently every day of the week
Calculations are banned in the field of tribology

items.explain: Because the interactions are so complex, empirical methods are often easier for analysis and theory.

items.prompt: Joule spun a paddle wheel in a vat of water and watched the water's temperature. What was he pinning down?

options.label: How much water a paddle wheel can lift
How fast heat travels through a vat of water
How much mechanical work produces a given amount of heat
How thick a fluid has to be to stop a wheel

items.explain: Joule specified a numerical value for the work needed to produce a unit of heat, using friction of a paddle wheel in water.
